answer: Stake-bonded registration resists Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to anchor its public key to a time-locked escrow deposit that peers verify before accepting requests and slash upon provable equivocation. Because each identity locks scarce liquid capital and risks forfeiture, adversaries cannot raise a knoll of free clones and face a hard basalt cost per active key. However, high collateral requirements exclude low-budget agents while wealthy attackers can still fund multiple slots.
